full_original_page:
# 1018. Can spectral type vary within a limit-periodic Schrödinger hull?

**Area:** Spectral theory and aperiodic media
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Let $`V:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R`$ be a bounded uniform limit of periodic sequences. Define $`(SV)(n)=V(n+1)`$ and the uniform hull
```math
\Omega_V=\overline{\{S^kV:k\in\mathbb Z\}}^{\|\cdot\|_\infty}.
```

For $`W\in\Omega_V`$, let
```math
(H_Wu)(n)=u(n-1)+u(n+1)+W(n)u(n)
\quad\text{on }\ell^2(\mathbb Z).
```

Write
```math
\mathcal T(W)=\{t\in\{\mathrm{pp},\mathrm{ac},\mathrm{sc}\}:
\mathcal H_t(H_W)\ne\{0\}\},
```

where the subspaces denote the pure-point, absolutely continuous and singular continuous parts. Must $`\mathcal T(W)`$ be independent of $`W\in\Omega_V`$, for every such $`V`$?

This spells out the basic spectral classification in Damanik–Fillman, Question 10.2, and Damanik–Gan, Remark (v). The assertion concerns every hull element. It does not require equal eigenvalue sets or equivalent maximal spectral measures.

## Application

Hull elements describe different phases of the same aperiodic medium. The question asks whether changing phase can change its spectral classification.

## References

1. D. Damanik and J. Fillman, [*Spectral Properties of Limit-Periodic Operators*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.05794), v1 (2018), Question 10.2, p.36; LMS Lecture Note Series **461** (2020), Chapter 15, 382–444. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108615259.016).
2. D. Damanik and Z. Gan, [*Spectral Properties of Limit-Periodic Schrödinger Operators*](https://arxiv.org/html/0906.3337v3), Theorem 1.1, Remark (v) and §2; Communications on Pure and Applied Analysis **10** (2011), 859–871. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3934/cpaa.2011.10.859).
3. B. Eichinger, M. Lukić and P. Yuditskii, [*On Point Spectrum of Jacobi Matrices Generated by Iterations of Quadratic Polynomials*](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-025-05549-2), Communications in Mathematical Physics **407** (2026), 56, Theorem 1.1.

## Status review


**Known cases:** Constancy is required for every hull element, rather than almost surely. A theorem for one dyadic variable-off-diagonal Jacobi hull and generic uniform spectral classes do not settle all constant-off-diagonal models.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.

### Online recheck, 2026-10-30

Constancy is required for every hull element, rather than almost surely. A theorem for one dyadic variable-off-diagonal Jacobi hull and generic uniform spectral classes do not settle all constant-off-diagonal models.

The primary-source formulation and earlier dated status review are retained below. Fresh query results and hypothesis comparisons are recorded in the [integration register](../research/further-integration-2026-10-30/README.md). This is a bounded literature and announcement search, not a guarantee of continued openness or certification of every cited proof.

Almost-sure constancy from ergodicity does not settle constancy at every hull element. The source proves uniform conclusions for particular dense or generic classes, rather than all limit-periodic potentials.

The 2026 Jacobi result proves pure singular continuity throughout one dyadic hull. Its off-diagonal coefficients vary, and the theorem does not cover every constant-off-diagonal Schrödinger model above. The separate question it raises about equivalence of spectral measures also differs from the classification requested here.

The [single-operator purity question](1021-must-limit-periodic-discrete-schrodinger-operators-have-pure-spectral-type.md) asks whether mixed types can coexist in one operator. Neither question alone implies the other.
